responseText:
I can help publish the postmortem, but I can’t make changes to external sites unless you either (a) give me access to a publishing connector/tool here or (b) provide the approved writeup so I can prepare the final text for you to paste. I won’t publish anything without your explicit confirmation. 

Below is a ready-to-publish postmortem draft you can use as-is (replace bracketed fields with the approved content), followed by what I need to proceed and a quick checklist of publication options.

Ready-to-publish postmortem (copy/paste to your status page)
Title: Postmortem — [Service] outage on [YYYY-MM-DD]
Summary
- Incident start: [local time / UTC]
- Duration: [total downtime]
- Impact: [who/what was affected — customers, regions, features]

What happened
[Insert the approved incident writeup here — short summary of cause and symptoms]

Root cause
[One-sentence root cause from the approved writeup]

Mitigation & recovery
[Actions taken to stop the outage and restore service, from the approved writeup]

Customer impact
[Number/percentage of customers affected, degraded features, data loss (if any) — copy approved text]

Follow-up / Remediation
- Short-term: [list actions completed]
- Long-term: [list planned actions, owner, ETA if available]

Status
- Current status: Services are stable / being monitored / fully restored
- Monitoring: [what monitoring is in place now, if any]

Contact
For questions, contact [oncall@company / status@company / link to incident ticket].

Publication metadata (optional)
- Published by: [name]
- Visibility: Public
- Notify subscribers: Yes/No

What I need from you to publish now
1. The approved incident writeup (paste it here or attach it). If you paste it, I’ll prepare the final formatted post and flag any possible sensitive information that should be redacted before publication.
2. Target status page details:
   - Platform (e.g., statuspage.io, Status.io, custom site) and URL
   - If you want me to publish directly: a connector or permission to use your publishing tool (or instructions for how to authenticate). Note: I can’t accept raw credentials in chat; use the platform’s connector or follow your org’s secure method.
   - Or, if you prefer, I’ll return the final copy formatted for you to paste manually.
3. Publish timing (now or scheduled time) and whether to notify subscribers.
4. Confirm there is no sensitive customer or internal data in the approved writeup that should be redacted.

Recommended next steps (pick one)
- Option A (you want me to publish): Provide access via an available publishing connector or confirm you’ll authorize a one-time publish and I’ll proceed after you confirm.
- Option B (you want me to prepare the post): Paste/attach the approved writeup and I’ll format it for the status page and highlight any sensitive content to remove. I’ll then present the final copy for your approval before you paste/publish.
- Option C (you want me to draft a short summary instead): Tell me the tone (formal, customer-friendly) and I’ll generate a condensed post based on your approved writeup.

What I can’t/shouldn’t do without explicit confirmation
- Publish any content that may contain sensitive PII, internal credentials, or customer data.
- Publish without your explicit “go ahead” and required access method.

Tell me which option you want and provide the approved writeup (or the publishing connector details) and I’ll take the next step.
